LPM0: Orai = short of Parmatma, apart from Parmatma.
(That person becomes convinced that) apart from Parmatma no one else is able to do anything,
In this world, no one accomplishes anything by himself.

UKJJ: O Nanak! This whole visible world has come forth from Parmatma alone. ||51||

Nanak, everything has been done by the Lord.
Sri Guru ji says: everything has come from that Prabhu alone. ||51|| ☬ Let us pray to Him like this:
K5TZ: Na chhootiai = cannot be cleared, cannot get out from under the debt of vices.

Because of the balance due on his account, he can never be released; he makes mistakes each and every moment.
In view of his account the mortal can never be released since the errs every moment.
By keeping accounts there is no release anywhere, because we make mistakes moment by moment.
2XE5: O Nanak! (Say:) O forgiving Prabhu! You Yourself forgive our mistakes, and carry us (who are drowning in the ocean of vices) across. ||1||
O Forgiving Lord, please forgive me, and carry Nanak across. ||1||
O you Pardoner, pardon me and ferry Nanak across the world-ocean.
O forgiving Vahiguru, forgive! Sri Guru ji says: and carry us across the world-ocean. ||1||
TS6G: Loon harami = one who betrays the salt he has eaten, ungrateful, thankless. Begana = a stranger, one who forms no bond. Alap = little.
A person is ungrateful, a sinner, shallow-minded; he stays a stranger to Parmatma;
The sinner is unfaithful to himself; he is ignorant, with shallow understanding.
The man is untrue to His salt and a sinner. He is ignorant and of paltry understanding.
O Maharaj! I am ungrateful, a sinner, (begana) ignorant, and of petty understanding.
5W8D: Jiu = life. Pind = body. Tah = Him. Tat = the origin (of life and body).
he does not even recognise that source, the Prabhu who gave him this life and body.

Who gave him soul body and comfort Him, the Essence of all he knows not.
You, who gave me life and body and every comfort — I do not know Your essential form.
TP0H: Laha = profit. Dah dis = in all ten directions.
For the sake of earning Maya he goes about searching in all ten directions,
For the sake of personal profit and Maya, he goes out, searching in the ten directions.
For the sake of worldly gain he goes searching in ten directions.
For the profit of Maya they go searching in the ten directions.
WNAZ: Nimakh = {nimesh} the time of a blink of the eye. Manah = in the mind.
but the Prabhu, the Giver, who is able to give everything — he does not keep Him in his mind even for the blink of an eye.

Lord the Bounteous Bestower he enshrines not in his mind, even for an instant.
O Prabhu, the generous Giver! They do not keep You in the mind for even a moment.
UQY7: Greed, falsehood, vices, and attachment to Maya — that is all; this is the wealth a person keeps stored in his mind.
Greed, falsehood, corruption and emotional attachment - these are what he collects within his mind.
Avarice, falsehood, sin and worldly love these he amasses within his mind.
Greed, falsehood, and the vices such as attachment — this is the wealth that is in my mind.
10ZD: Lampat = given to sensual pleasure. Bihai = life passes.
His life passes in the company of those who are given to sensual pleasure, thieves, great slanderers.
The worst perverts, thieves and slanderers - he passes his time with them.
The great libertines thieves and slanderers with them he passes his life.
The span of life keeps passing in the company of those who are lustful, thieves and great slanderers.
FCCS: (But, O Prabhu!) If it pleases You, You Yourself keep the counterfeit in the company of the genuine and forgive them.
But if it pleases You, Lord, then You forgive the counterfeit along with the genuine.
If it pleases You, O Lord then You forgivest the counterfeit along with the genuine.
O Bhagvan! If it pleases You, You forgive the counterfeit and join them with the genuine.
F5KM: Pahan = stones, stone-hearted people. Neer = in the water, with the amrit of the Name. ||52||
O Nanak! If it pleases Parmatma, He saves people who have become stone-hearted (in their thinking), giving them the gift of the amrit of the Name (from drowning in the waves of vices). ||52||
O Nanak, if it pleases the Supreme Lord God, then even a stone will float on water. ||52||
Nanak, provided it be pleasing to the Supreme Lord the stone floats on water.
Sri Guru ji says: O (Parbrahm) Vahiguru! When it pleases You, (pahan) stones float on water — that is, even the worst sinners are carried across. ||52||
955B: O Prabhu! We beings, eating and drinking only the things of Maya, laughing and playing only in the colours and shows of Maya, have come wandering through countless life-forms;
Eating, drinking, playing and laughing, I have wandered through countless incarnations.
In eating drinking, playing and laughing have I wandered in many births.
Through khakha he says: eating, drinking, playing and laughing, we kept wandering through countless births.
Z0UR: O Nanak! (Say:) You Yourself draw us out of the world-ocean; we have Your support alone. ||1||
Please, God, lift me up and out of the terrifying world-ocean. Nanak seeks Your Support. ||1||
Take me out of the terrible world-ocean my Master. Nanak has Your support alone.
So, O Prabhu! Draw me out of the world-ocean. Sri Guru ji says: I have come to Your (tek) refuge. ||1||
N84A: Khelat khelat = amusing the mind again and again.
Amusing his mind in the colours of Maya, a person comes passing through countless life-forms, suffering as he goes.
Playing, playing, I have been reincarnated countless times, but this has only brought pain.
Sporting, playing and suffering pain in many existences I have come as human being.
Suffering in countless life-forms, I have come playing — that is, wandering and wandering.
8BLJ: Khed = suffering and trouble. Sadhu = the Guru. Samai = absorbed, with the attention joined.
If the Guru is met, if the attention is joined to the Guru's words, then all suffering and trouble is wiped out.
Troubles are removed, when one meets with the Holy; immerse yourself in the Word of the True Guru.
Troubles are removed by meeting the Saint and being absorbed in True Guru's instruction.
On meeting the sadhu, all (khed) suffering has ceased, and through the words — that is, the teaching — of the Satguru, I have merged into Vahiguru.
4S5R: Gahi = held, took up. Sanchio = gathered. Khaio = made one's food.
The one who (from the Guru's door) took up a forgiving nature, gathered the wealth of the Name, and made the amrit of the Name his spiritual food —
Adopting an attitude of tolerance, and gathering truth, partake of the Ambrosial Nectar of the Name.
Adopting forbearance and amassing truth man partakes of the Name Nectar.

I have taken up forgiveness, and (sanchio) gathered the true wealth of the Name, and eaten — that is, made my food — only the Name, which is amrit; the meaning is, I have held the Name in the heart and repeated only the Name.
WFZQ: on him is Parmatma's great grace; he stays settled in spiritual bliss and peace.
When my Lord and Master showed His Great Mercy, I found peace, happiness and bliss.
When the Lord showed His great mercy, I found haven in joy and happiness.
The Thakur's grace has been (khari) very great, for I have found (bisram) a settled place in the bliss of the self and in worldly comforts.
GD0R: Khep = trade, dealings. Ghar aae = settled within the inner self. Pativant = honoured.
The person who (having learned the way from the Guru) carried the trade (of praise) through to the end (all his life) earned profit; (saved from wandering) he becomes steady in mind and earns honour.
My merchandise has arrived safely, and I have made a great profit; I have returned home with honor.
My merchandise has safely arrived, I have made good profit and have returned home with honour.
Vahiguru has carried through our devotion — or this trade that is the Bani. When we came and reached the home of the true form, then we became honoured.
L3RR: Gur = the Guru. Dilasa = comfort for the heart.
The Guru gave him still greater comfort of heart, and he was joined to Bhagvan's feet.
The Guru has given me great consolation, and the Lord God has come to meet me.
Great is the consolation the Guru has given me and the illustrious Lord has come and met me.
When the Guru gave us (khara) great (dilasa) reassurance, then Bhagvan ji came and met me.
RL64: Aagai pachhai = in this world and the next.
(But all this is the Prabhu's grace.) O Prabhu! You made this whole play; even now You alone are doing everything. In this world and the next You Yourself are the protector of beings.
He Himself has acted, and He Himself acts. He was in the past, and He shall be in the future.
God Himself acted and Himself acts He was in the past and Himself shall be in future.
(Pachhai) in the past Vahiguru Himself did everything; now in the present He Himself is doing it; and (aagai) in the future too Vahiguru Himself will do it.
26YD: Sarahiai = let us praise, let us sing the praises. ||53||
O Nanak! We should always praise that Prabhu alone, who is present in every body. ||53||
O Nanak, praise the One, who is contained in each and every heart. ||53||
Nanak, praise Him alone who is contained in every heart.
So Sri Guru ji says: let us praise (sou) that very Vahiguru, the Parmeshvar who fills all hearts. ||53||
K6TK: O Prabhu! O treasure of grace! O Merciful One! We have come to Your refuge.
O God, I have come to Your Sanctuary, O Merciful Lord, Ocean of compassion.
My Merciful Master the Ocean of Compassion I have entered Yours sanctuary.
The people who have reached the refuge of the Prabhu, the ocean of grace —
2AH9: Akhar = {akshar} 1. the imperishable Prabhu; 2. the Prabhu's command. Man = in the mind. Nihal = delighted, blossoming. ||1||
O Nanak! (Say:) those in whose minds the one imperishable Prabhu stays dwelling — their minds stay ever blossoming. ||1||
One whose mind is filled with the One Word of the Lord, O Nanak, becomes totally blissful. ||1||

in their minds the one (akhar) imperishable, merciful Hari dwells. Sri Guru ji says: those beings have become (nihal) free of suffering. Or: of the fifty-two letters spoken here to set forth Hari, the person in whose mind Hari comes to dwell through the teaching of even one letter — that being becomes blissful. ||1||
AEJS: Akhar meh = within the command. Prabh = the Prabhu. Dhare = established.
The Prabhu created these three worlds (the whole world) within His command.
In the Word, God established the three worlds.
In the Lord's word is the installation of the three worlds.
The Prabhu Parmeshvar, who is (akhar) imperishable — or who is in the letters — holds the three worlds within Himself.
WBBX: Akhar kar = by the command, through the command. Kar bed = having made the Vedas.
By the Prabhu's command alone the Vedas were composed and reflected on.
Created from the Word, the Vedas are contemplated.
By joining together the words the Vedas are studied.
Through (akhar) Parmeshvar, or through the letters, the reflection on the Vedas is going on.
Z64D: All the Shastras, Simritis and Puranas are the expression of the Prabhu's command.
From the Word, came the Shaastras, Simritees and Puraanas.
The words tell what is written in Shashtras, Simritis and Puranas.
The Shastras, the Simritis and the Puranas, all together, are the very form of the letters.
MSA4: Nad = sound, raag, kirtan. Vakhyana = teaching, exposition.
The kirtan, discourse and exposition of these Puranas, Shastras and Simritis are also the manifestation of the Prabhu's command.
From the Word, came the sound current of the Naad, speeches and explanations.
In letters are written the hymns discourses and lectures.
(Nad) music and (kathan) discourse — all these the great souls have (vakhyana) spoken as the form of the letters.
692H: Finding release from the fears and doubts of the world is also the light of the Prabhu's command.
From the Word, comes the way of liberation from fear and doubt.
By means of letters is described the way of escape from dread and doubt.
The way to liberation, and doubt too, are the form of the letters.
MTY5: Kirat = {kritya} what ought to be done.
Recognising the deeds worth doing (in human life), seeking the rules of spiritual purity — this too is a sight of the Prabhu's command.
From the Word, come religious rituals, karma, sacredness and Dharma.
The words narrate the religious rites worldly acts piety and religion.
And the (kirat) doing of deeds, and the whole body of (such) pure duties that come with the divisions of caste and stage of life — all are the form of the letters.
WV23: Akhar hai = is (the expanse) of the Akhar, the expanse of the command.

In the visible universe, the Word is seen.
In the entire visible world is contained the Indestructible Lord.

The final conclusion is this: the whole world-show that comes into sight is the form of the letters. ☬ If one asks: being the form of everything, will He share in merit and sin, and so become a jiva? To this Sri Guru ji says:
VZZS: but, O Nanak, the Prabhu (the Master of the command) Himself is beyond the reach (of this whole expanse). ||54||
O Nanak, the Supreme Lord God remains unattached and untouched. ||54||
Nevertheless, O Nanak, the Supreme Lord remains unattached.

Parbrahm Parmeshvar is in truth (nirlepa) unattached. Or: this whole visible world is in the letters; Sri Guru ji says: those letters are the form of the perfect, unattached Brahm. ||54|| ☬ Bringing the Bani to its close, he prays:
26X0: Hath = in the hand. Agamm = unreachable. Agamm hath = in the hand of the unreachable Hari. Mastak = on the forehead.

The Inaccessible Lord with pen in His hand scribed man's destiny on his forehead.
O Vahiguru, (agamm) beyond mind and speech! In Your hand is the pen of command, which keeps writing destinies on the foreheads of beings.
WR31: Urajh rahio = is interwoven (like warp and weft). Anoop = beautiful. Roopavati = possessed of form.

The Lord of Incomparable Beauty is involved with all.
The Lord of peerless beauty is contained with (among) all.
And You are (urajh) entangled — that is, woven like warp and weft — with all, and Your being is of a form beyond compare.
FUJT: O Prabhu! I cannot describe Your greatness with my mouth.
I cannot describe Your Praises with my mouth, O Lord.
Yours praises O Lord I cannot describe with my mouth.
O Maharaj! Your praise cannot be spoken with the mouth; the meaning is that it is endless.
K67S: O Nanak! (Say:) seeing Your vision, my soul is enraptured; it is a sacrifice, a sacrifice to You. ||1||
Nanak is fascinated, gazing upon the Blessed Vision of Your Darshan; he is a sacrifice to You. ||1||
Nanak is fascinated on beholding Your sight and is devoted to You.
Seeing Your vision, my understanding is enchanted. Sri Guru ji says: my understanding goes as a sacrifice to You. ||1||
CVSW: Achut = {chyu = to fall} achyut, the One who never perishes. Agh = sin.
O Nanak! (Pray and say:) O Parmatma, You who never waver! O imperishable Prabhu! O destroyer of the sins of beings!
O Immovable Lord, O Supreme Lord God, Imperishable, Destroyer of sins:
O my Immovable and Imperishable Lord, O My Transcendent Lord the Destroyer of sin.
O (achut) unshakeable One! O Parbrahm! O imperishable One! O destroyer of sins!
KEJZ: Sarabmai = all-pervading. Guntas = treasure of virtues.
O perfect Prabhu, pervading all beings! O remover of the sufferings of beings! O treasure of virtues!
O Perfect, All-pervading Lord, Destroyer of pain, Treasure of virtue:
O You all-Pervading Perfect one. O You Destroyer of grief and Treasure of virtue.
O perfect One! O You whose form is the whole universe! O breaker of sufferings, ocean of virtues!
11MW: Nirankar = without form. Nirgun = apart from the three qualities of Maya.
O companion of all! (And yet) the formless Prabhu! O You who stay apart from the influence of Maya! O support of all beings!
O Companion, Formless, Absolute Lord, Support of all:
O mortal comrade, O formless One, O Absolute Lord the support of all.
O companion of all! O (nirankar) formless One! O (nirgun) One beyond the three qualities, the support of all!
XWJC: Nidhan = treasure. Bibek = the power to discern.
O You who care for creation! O treasure of virtues! You within whom the power of discernment is ever present!
O Lord of the Universe, Treasure of excellence, with clear eternal understanding:
O Supporter of earth, O the ocean of excellences, who art ever possessed of discrimination.
O Gobind! O ocean of virtues! (Ja kai) You whose virtues are ever being (bibek) reflected on — or, You who ever have knowledge!
B48N: Aparampar = beyond the beyond. Hah bhi = are present now too.
O Prabhu, beyond the beyond! You are present now, and You are ever-abiding.
Most Remote of the Remote, Lord God: You are, You were, and You shall always be.
O Remotest of the remote Lord God, You are, wert and shall be.
O Hari, (aparampar) beyond all other beings! (Hare) You who give all beings their being and life-force — You are now, and You will be hereafter.
D8Y3: O ever the helper of the saints! O support of those without support!
O Constant Companion of the Saints, You are the Support of the unsupported.
O constant Companion of the Saints, You are the Support of the Supportless.
O You who are ever the companion of the saints! You are the support of the hopeless.
VB6X: Dasro = a humble little servant. Nirgun = without virtue.
O Sustainer of creation! I am Your humble little servant; I am without virtue; there is no virtue in me.
O my Lord and Master, I am Your slave. I am worthless, I have no worth at all.
O Lord, I am a servant of Yours. I am without merit. No merit do I possess.
O Thakur ji! I am Your servant. In me, the one without virtue, there is no virtue at all.

F0L0: Rakhau = I will keep. Hiai = in the heart. ||55||
Grant me the gift of Your Name; I will keep (this gift) strung in my heart. ||55||
Nanak: grant me the Gift of Your Name, Lord, that I may string it and keep it within my heart. ||55||
Grant me, Nanak the gift of Your Name, that I may string and keep it in my mind.
O Maharaj! Give me the gift of Your Name, for I will string it — that is, hold it — in my heart. ||55||
S1AX: The Guru alone is mother, the Guru alone is father (the Guru alone gives spiritual birth); the Guru is the form of the Master, the Prabhu.
The Divine Guru is our mother, the Divine Guru is our father; the Divine Guru is our Lord and Master, the Transcendent Lord.
The Divine Guru is my mother, the Divine Guru the father and the Divine Guru is my Lord and Supreme God.

The Guru, who is (dev) light itself — that is, a knower of the essence — is the form of mother and father. And the Guru-dev alone is the (suami) king, and the form of Parmeshvar; the one on whose support one's livelihood rests is also called master.
MVVZ: Sakha = friend. Agian bhanjan = destroyer of ignorance. Bandhip = kinsman. Sahodara = {sah + udar: born of the same mother's womb} brother.
The Guru is the friend who destroys the darkness (of attachment to Maya); the Guru alone is the kinsman and brother (who stands by to the end).
The Divine Guru is my companion, the Destroyer of ignorance; the Divine Guru is my relative and brother.
The Divine Guru is my companion, the dispeller of spiritual ignorance and the Divine Guru is my relative and brother.
The Guru-dev alone is the (sakha) friend, the destroyer of ignorance; and the Guru-dev is like a (sahodar) brother — that is, one born of the same womb.
53MW: Nirodhara = that which cannot be stopped, whose effect cannot be undone. Mant = teaching.
The Guru is the (real) giver, who teaches the Prabhu's Name; the Guru's teaching is such that (no vice or the like) can undo its effect.
The Divine Guru is the Giver, the Teacher of the Lord's Name. The Divine Guru is the Mantra which never fails.
The Divine Guru is the giver and the teacher of God's Name and the Divine Guru is my infallible spell.

The Guru-dev ji is the giver of the teaching of Hari's Name. The mantra of the Guru-dev ji (nirodhara) certainly — or especially — or without any other support, brings deliverance; the meaning is that it needs the help of no other ritual.
FXGB: Sat = truth, the ever-abiding Prabhu. Budh = understanding. Moorat = form. Paras = touch.
The Guru is the embodiment of peace, truth and understanding; the Guru is a philosopher's stone whose touch is higher than the touch of the philosopher's stone.
The Divine Guru is the image of peace, truth and wisdom. The Divine Guru is the Philosopher's Stone - touching it, one is transformed.
The Divine Guru is the images of peace truth and wisdom the Divine Guru is the philosopher's stone by touching which the mortal is saved.
The Guru-dev is the form of peace, truth and (budh) wisdom; and the Guru-dev's (paras) meeting is (para) greater even than the philosopher's stone.
FZRA: Amrit sarovar = pool of amrit. Majan = dip, bathing. Aparampara = beyond the beyond.
The Guru is the (true) pilgrimage place, the pool of amrit; bathing in (the water of) the Guru's wisdom is far higher (than bathing at all other pilgrimage places).
The Divine Guru is the sacred shrine of pilgrimage, and the pool of divine nectar; bathing in the Guru's wisdom, one experiences the Infinite.
The divine Guru is a place of pilgrimage and a tank of Nectar. By having a bath in Guru's Divine knowledge, man meets the Illimitable Master.

The Guru-dev is the (tirath) form of purity. Or: what kind of pilgrimage place? A pool of amrit — the meaning is, whoever keeps his company, he frees from birth and death. And the person who has bathed in the amrit of wisdom in the Guru-pool has attained Parmeshvar, (aparam) the form beyond Brahma and the rest.
LA3N: Sabh = all. Harta = remover. Patit = those fallen (into vices), the sinful. Pavit kara = the one who purifies.
The Guru is the form of the Creator, the remover of all sins; the Guru purifies (the hearts of) sinful people.
The Divine Guru is the Creator, and the Destroyer of all sins; the Divine Guru is the Purifier of sinners.
The Divine Guru is the Creator and the Destroyer of all the sins and the Divine Guru is the purifier of the impure.
The Guru-dev is the form of the Creator, the remover of all a being's sins; and the Guru-dev has purified (patit) sinners.
53RB: Jug jug = in every age. Jap = repeating. Udhara = one is saved (from the waves of vices in the world-ocean).

Since the world was made, from the very beginning, the Guru has been there in every age (as the giver of the teaching of Parmatma's Name). By repeating the mantra of Hari's Name given by the Guru, one crosses over (the waves of vices in the world-ocean).
The Divine Guru existed in the very beginning, throughout the ages, in each and every age. The Divine Guru is the Mantra of the Lord's Name; chanting it, one is saved.
The Divine Guru is from the beginning from the beginning of ages and in every age. The Divine Guru is the spell of God's Name by repeating which the mortal is saved.

The Guru-dev (aad jugad) was forever and ever in the past, will be in age after age to come, and is now. And the person who has repeated Hari through the Guru-dev's (mant) teaching has attained deliverance.
3UXV: Prabh = O Prabhu! Jit = through which. Jit lag = attached to which.
O Prabhu! Show grace; give us the company of the Guru, so that we foolish sinners may cross over (by staying) in his company.
O God, please be merciful to me, that I may be with the Divine Guru; I am a foolish sinner, but holding onto Him, I will be carried across.
My Master, take pity and unite me, a fool and a sinner, with the society of the Guru, by clinging to which I may swim across the sea of life.

O Prabhu! Casting Your glance of grace, unite me with the company of the Guru-dev. (Ham) the whole multitude — or the multitude of foolish sinners like me — has crossed over by (lag) joining with him; or: may I, joining him, cross over.
A9PT: The Guru is the form of the Parmesar, the Parbrahm. O Nanak! One should (always) bow to the Guru, who is Hari's form. ||1||
The Divine Guru is the True Guru, the Supreme Lord God, the Transcendent Lord; Nanak bows in humble reverence to the Lord, the Divine Guru. ||1||
The Divine Guru the True Guru is himself the Exalted Lord and the Great Lord. To the Godly Divine Guru. Nanak makes an obeisance.

The Satguru, who is (gur) worthy of worship and (dev) light itself, is the very form of Parbrahm Parmeshvar. So Sri Guru ji says: salutation to such a Guru-dev ji, who is Hari's form — or, salutation every time. ||1||

Read this Salok at the beginning, and at the end. ||
Read this slok in the beginning and at the end.

Of its twenty-four thousand letters — whoever recites or hears it, all the breaths that go out of him in the eight watches of the day become fruitful. And its greatness is great: it is the form of the jewel of peace. So now Sri Guru ji first utters the salutation to the Satgurus, the auspicious invocation of the soul:

In Gauri Pearl of peace 5th Guru.
6JS7: Akal Purakh is One, and He is met through the grace of the Satguru.
One Universal Creator God. By The Grace Of The True Guru:
There is but One God. By the True Guru's grace He is obtained.
6PW0: Namah = salutation. Gurae = to the greatest (of all). Adi = the beginning (of all).
(My) salutation is to that greatest (Akal Purakh) who is the beginning (of all),
I bow to the Primal Guru.
I bow to the Primordial Guru.
To the primal Guru, the first Guru Nanak Sahib Ji, is our salutation.
KQSY: Jugadi = (He who) is from the beginning of the ages.
and who is from the beginning of the ages.
I bow to the Guru of the ages.
I bow to the Guru of the primal age.

VHFF: I bow to the True Guru.
I make obeisance to the True Guru.

(when) you become old, (then) He makes ready kinsmen and friends to serve you,

(O being!) By whose (the Lord's) grace you dwell in comfort upon the earth,
By His Grace, you abide in comfort upon the earth.
By whose grace, you residest in comfort on the earth,
O brother! By whose grace, Vahiguru's, you dwell upon the earth together with comfort.
DT6V: Sut = son. Bhrat = brother. Banita = wife. Hasah = you laugh.
you laugh with son, brother, friend and wife;
With your children, siblings, friends and spouse, you laugh.
and laughest with yours sons, brothers, friend and wife.

G420: By whose mercy you drink cool water,
By His Grace, you drink in cool water.
By whose favour you drinkest cool water,
By whose grace you drink cool water.
P9FX: (you use) the comfort-giving air and the priceless fire;

and havest soothing wind and priceless fire,
Again, He has given you the air and the priceless fire as comfort-giving.
XFNB: By whose grace you enjoy all the relishes,
By His Grace, you enjoy all sorts of pleasures.
By whose favour, you enjoyest all pleasure
By whose grace you enjoy all the relishes.
8ZQ2: you dwell together with all things (the sense being, all things come to you for your use);
You are provided with all the necessities of life.
and livest with all the necessaries.
Again, the gathering, that is the whole collection, of the materials of all substances dwells together with you.
C7DG: Hasat = hands. Pav = feet. Karan = ears. Netra = eyes. Rasna = tongue.
(He who) has given you hands, feet, ears, eyes and tongue,
He gave you hands, feet, ears, eyes and tongue,
Who gave you hands, feet, ears, eyes and tongue.
That Vahiguru who has given you hands, feet, ears, eyes, tongue and the other senses.
R6T7: Tisah = Him (the Lord). Tiag = having abandoned, having forgotten. Rachna = you are engrossed, you are absorbed.
forgetting that (Lord), (O being!) you are engrossed with others.
and yet, you forsake Him and attach yourself to others.
You forsakest Him and attachest yourself to others
Abandoning the remembrance of Him, you are engrossed together with others. ☬ Let the being make supplication in this manner:
GFD6: Dokh = evil deeds. Murh = the foolish being. Biape = are entangled.
(These) foolish, blind beings (who cast aside His goodness) are caught in such faults.
Such sinful mistakes cling to the blind fools;

The aforesaid faults cling to the foolish and ignorant one.
S4UB: O Nanak! (Make supplication for these beings, and say) — O Lord! Pull (them) out Yourself (from these faults). ||2||
Nanak: uplift and save them, God! ||2||
Nanak, you Yourself save him, O Lord.

B8D5: Ad = from the beginning (that is, from the time of birth). Ant = to the end (that is, till death).
He who is the protector (of this being) from its birth right up to the time of death,
From beginning to end, He is our Protector,
He, who is Protector of all from beginning to end,
That Vahiguru who is the protector of you at the beginning in the mother's womb, and at the end in the world beyond from the messengers of death.
ZVJL: the foolish man does not make love with that Lord.
and yet, the ignorant do not give their love to Him.
Him, the ignorant man loves not.
O boor! You do not make love together with Him.
QXN8: Ja ki = whose (the Lord's). Nav nidh = the nine treasures.
by whose service (this being) obtains the nine treasures (of the world),
Serving Him, the nine treasures are obtained,
From whose, service, he obtains the nine treasures,
By the doing of whose service you would obtain the nine treasures.

the foolish being does not join his mind with that Lord.
and yet, the foolish do not link their minds with Him.
with Him, the fool attaches not his mind.
O fool! You are not attaching your mind together with Him.
7YDM: Hajure = present and witnessing, ever at hand.
who at every moment is beside it,
Our Lord and Master is Ever-present, forever and ever,
The Lord who is, ever and ever, just present,
That Thakur who (sad sada) at all times is present and manifest before you, that is, ever at your side.
YBJ3: the blind man reckons that Thakur to be (sitting) far away (somewhere).

O blind being! You know Him to be far off.
S1KP: by whose service it obtains honour in (the Lord's) court,

By the doing of whose service you would obtain honour in (dargah) the world beyond.
8JL5: Tisah = Him (the Lord). Mugadh = the fool.

and yet, the ignorant fool forgets Him.
O fool! Through ignorance you forget Him here.

Let him make supplication in this manner: O Hari! This being, before and after, is ever the one to go astray.
F4D6: O Nanak! The Lord who protects is infinite (He does not look to the faults of this being). ||3||
O Nanak, the Infinite Lord is our Saving Grace. ||3||
Nanak, the infinite Lord is the only Saviour.
Sri Guru Ji says: O infinite Lord! You alone are its protector.
HKZY: (The Maya-ridden being), leaving the jewel (of the Name), goes about delighting in the cowrie (in the form of Maya).

Abandoning a jewel, man is engrossed with a shell.
This being, abandoning the jewel of detachment, is engrossed in, that is makes love with, trifling substances like a cowrie.

And abandoning (sach) the Name, he is blazing together with the false lusts and the rest, that is, he flourishes.

That body which is to be left and gone from, that he reckons as everlasting.

that (death) which must certainly befall, he imagines to be (sitting) far away (somewhere).
That which is immanent, they believe to be far off.
What is to happen, he recognises that to be distant.
And that dying which is bound to come to be, that he recognizes as far off.
KTB9: Tis ka = of that, for the sake of that. Sram = labour, toil.
For the sake of that (wealth and goods) which (in the end) is to be left behind, he goes about toiling (every day);

What he has to part, he toils after that.
That Maya which is to be left and gone from — for the gathering of those things he undergoes hardship.

the (Lord) who is the protector with (him), Him he has forgotten.

He spurns the Succourer who is ever with him.
And that Parmeshvar who is to be his helper, Him he abandons.

This being's doings and conduct are those of a beast, and his caste is that of a man.

He humbugs people day and night.
He keeps making a (pachara) display before people day and night.

Outwardly, they wear religious robes, but within is the filth of Maya.
Outwardly wearing religious garbs, inwardly has the filth of worldliness.
Outwardly he has made a bright garb, and within the heart the filth in the form of Maya keeps clinging.

though the effort be made to hide it (with the outward garb), (the mind's filth) is not hidden.

But however much this being may make concealment from Vahiguru, or from people, the deed, though concealed, is not concealed, the sense being that it becomes manifest.

Outwardly he does the talk of knowledge, and out of hypocrisy the meditation and the bathing, for the sake of display.
BQXT: Biapai = is exerting its force. Suan = a dog.
but within the mind the dog (in the form) of greed is exerting its force.
but within clings the dog of greed.

And within the heart the dog in the form of greed is holding sway.
A31L: Within the mind is the fire (of craving), outwardly the body is (smeared) with ashes;

Within the heart is the fire in the form of craving, and outwardly ashes have been smeared upon the body.

There is a stone around their neck - how can they cross the unfathomable ocean?
With the stone around his neck how can he cross the unfathomable ocean?
And about the neck he has kept bound the stone in the form of sins; so how will he cross the unfathomable ocean of the world, that is, he will not cross it.
TX1Z: Ja kai antar = within whose heart.
Each and every man within whose heart the Lord comes to dwell —
Those, within whom God Himself abides
He, within whose heart the Lord Himself abides,
Therefore, he within whom the Lord Himself comes and dwells, the sense being, he who makes remembrance of Him —
EMLG: Sahaj = in poise, in that state where the mind does not waver. Samat = merges, becomes settled. ||5||

- O Nanak, those humble beings are intuitively absorbed in the Lord. ||5||

By hearing alone, how can the blind man find the path?
As when someone has said, go off in the direction of such and such a tree — then, hearing that voice, how will that blind man find the road? That is, he cannot find it.

Take his hand he shall reach the destination.

But if some compassionate person takes hold of his hand and leads him, then it goes through to the end, that is, he arrives. But when You, showing grace, take hold of the hand in the form of the mind, then he arrives at the goal.
YTHM: Bujharat = a sign, a gesture. Dora = deaf.

How can a riddle be understood by the deaf?
How can a deaf man understand the riddle?
And how will the (dora) deaf man understand the sign? That is, he does not understand it.

That which in the Ved was a sign for entering upon the path of withdrawal, that some have understood as a reading within the path of engagement alone; as, for instance, it is written that wine and flesh are to be brought into the sacrifice, and beings have understood this as their consumption, whereas the Ved's intent lay in having them renounced.

T17B: Karuna = pity. Karuna mai = full of pity, the one who shows mercy (Note = Skt. मय (Punjabi 'mai') is an affix used to indicate 'made of, consisting of,' 'full of'). Din = the meek (being).

Within the body which is perishable in an instant, like a house of sand, this being dwells.

He enjoys sports and pleasures of wealth.
Reckoning it to be the giver of (kel) sports of the form of bliss, he has become (rasai) one with the love of Maya.

To this fool death does not come to mind.

to Him ever make an obeisance.
to Him alone let us make obeisance for ever.

He in whose mind the Lord's Name becomes sweet, that is dear —
